To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CaMKIV and calcineurin are both involved in the regulation of the PGC- 1α gene, that MEF2s are involved in the positive feedback regulation of PGC- 10, and that PGC-1a is involved in the positive regulation of MEF2s.
PGC-1 α expression is regulated by both calcium/calmodulin kinase IV and calcineurin, and that a positive feedback exists between PGC1α and members in the MEF2 family of transcription factors.
CaMKIV, calcineurin, and PGC-1a form an autoregulatory feedback loop, which may contribute to the relatively stable phenotype of skeletal muscle fiber types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanism that regulates the expression of PGC1α and its role in the regulation of muscle fiber types.
the transcriptional regulation of the key regulator PGC-1a.
the regulation of PGC-α and its role in muscle fiber type determination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium-signaling pathways are important for the expression of PGC1α in skeletal muscle.
the calcium-signaling pathways, CaMKIV and calcineurin, activate the transcription factor MEF2, which, in turn, activates PGC- 1α, which, in a positive feedback loop, activates MEF2.
the calcium-signaling components CaMKIV and calcineurin regulate the expression of the transcriptional coactivator PGC-1, which in turn activates the transcription of MEF2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the calcium-signaling pathways and the PGC-α pathway are tightly integrated and that the calcium pathway is the primary regulator of the PGC- α pathway, whereas the PGC- 1α pathway is the secondary regulator of the calcium pathway.
the calcium signaling pathway, through CaMKIV and calcineurin, regulates PGC-1alpha expression, which in turn regulates MEF2 activity.

PGC-1alpha is a key regulator of skeletal muscle fiber-type switching and that the PGC1alpha promoter is regulated by the calcium-signaling pathways, which may be involved in muscle adaptation to chronic exercise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PGC-1a is a key regulator in skeletal muscle fiber type determination, and it is regulated by CaMKIV and MEF2.
the calcium signaling pathway and the transcriptional switch, PGC-1alpha, are integrated into a positive feedback loop.
calcium signaling is a major regulator of PGC- 1α expression, and PGC-1 α in turn is a major regulator for MEF2s.
